issue.title: ignore unreadable directories

labels.name: archived due to age
labels.description: This issue has been archived; please open a new issue for any further discussion

repository.name: eslint
repository.description: Find and fix problems in your JavaScript code.

issue.body: I'm not sure if this is the best fix, but the issue that happens is that eslint tries to find eslintrc, and traverses up the directory tree.  If it encounters a directory that it cannot read, then eslint will crash.  For example, this happens with flycheck in emacs with pam_tmpdir (since flycheck saves the file to a temporary directory, and pam_tmpdir manages secure per-user temporary directories), but I suppose this could also happen if the user only has execute permissions on /home.

body: What would you expect it to do instead of crashing?

As far as I can tell, there are two behaviours that would be acceptable:
1. give up looking for eslint, under the assumption than if the user can't read the directory, they don't own any of the ancestors, so there probably won't be a valid eslintrc to find.
2. (this is what my proposed patch does) ignore the unreadable directory, and keep traversing up the directory tree

I don't think silently ignoring the error is the correct way to go - it seems like this is something the user should be notified about in some way. The question is, do we abort completely or output some kind of warning? Or something else?

I don't think it should abort, since that would break eslint on valid (albeit uncommon) setups.  Since it can be triggered by valid setups, and, as far as I can tell, there's no way to distinguish between invalid and valid setups, I don't know if there is a sensible notification that can be given to the user.  Mind you, I am not completely opposed to emitting a warning.  I just don't see the need.
Why would a valid setup instruct ESLint to search in a directory that it wouldn't be able to read?

If ESLint is _instructed by the user_ to search in a directory that cannot be read, then I agree that this is an error.  However, the issue is that ESLint searches for the eslintrc file _by itself_ by traversing up the directory tree, and during this traversal, it can encounter an unreadable directory which causes an error.
For example if the permissions /home are: --x--x--x (i.e. users only have execute permissions, which prevents users from listing the contents of /home, but still allows them to open files/subdirectories of /home if they have the appropriate permissions on those files/subdirectories), and with the regular permissions on the user's home directories, then is user1 tries running ESLint on /home/user1/foo.js, then ESLint will try to find eslintrc in /home/user1, and (if it doesn't find it in /home/user1) then in /home.  But when it tries to read /home, then the readDirSync throws an exception because the user isn't allowed to list the contents of /home, and then ESLint crashes.

Ah okay, I get it now. I somehow completely missed that we were talking about `.eslintrc` file lookup (I'm going to go ahead and blame my being really sick for the past two weeks, but really I was probably just reading your comments too quickly). What you're saying makes total sense now.
Oops, meant to close the PR, not the issue.
